questions.question: Banking comes under which sector of economic growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Tertiary Sector__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Primary Sector:

 
 
• It includes the extraction of raw materials.
 
• It includes agricultural and allied activities.
 
• Examples of the primary sector include Farming, Fishing, Coal mining, Oil extraction, Diamond mining, etc.
 
 
 
• Secondary Sector:
 
 
• It includes the production of finished goods and components. 
 
• Examples of the secondary sector include turning metals into tools and automobiles, Refining petroleum into gasoline, and energy production, etc.
 
 
 
• ​Tertiary Sector:__
 __
 
• It includes commercial services.
 
• Examples of the Tertiary sector include Restaurants, **Banking,**__ School teachers, Tourism, etc.
 
 
 
• Quaternary Sector:
 
 
• It is related to ICT and research development.
 
• Examples of the Quaternary sector include research and development, data processing, financial services, etc.

questions.question:
Which of the following economic activities comes under primary sector?

I. Fishing

II. Dairy

III. Agriculture
questions.solution:
• Primary sector in economic activity deals with the production and collection of raw materials.
 
• Fishing, Dairy and Agriculture are all examples of primary sector as they provide us with the raw materials such as fish, milk , cereals respectively.

questions.question: In which of the following legislation can be initiated?

options.text: Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Neither Lok Sabha nor Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:
• The legislative system follows a proper protocol for the process of law making.
 
• The initial step in this protocol involves introduction of a bill (draft for the law) in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• It is only after the approval from both the houses that the bill (non-money bill) is officially made into the law.

questions.question: According to which fundamental right ‘human trafficking’ is prohibited?
questions.solution:
• Right against Exploitation states that no individual can be exploited by another person, that is, forced to do something illegal and against their will.
 
• It is stated under the Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan ‘Do or Die’?
questions.solution:
• While addressing Indian National Congress delegates at a meeting in Bombay on 8thAugust 1942, Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan ‘Do or Die'.
 
• The meeting was a part of the Quit India Movement which resolved to end the British rule in India.

questions.question: Who was the first Mughal Emperor in india?
questions.solution:
• Babur was the first Mughal emperor in India.
 
• He founded the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi in 1526.
 
• He died on 26th December 1530 and was succeeded by Humayun.
 
•

questions.question: What is the approximate distance (in million km) of the Sun from the Earth?
questions.solution:
• Earth is the third planet from the Sun and it is at a distance of approximately 150 million kilometres from the Sun.
 
• This distance is called the Astronomical Unit.
 
• This unit is used to measure greater distances. For instance, Jupitor is 5.2 AU away from the Sun, which implies that Jupiter is 5.2*150 million that is, 780 million kilometres from the Sun.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent by area of Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With a surface area of approximately **44 million km2 Asia is the largest continent on Earth**.
 
• It is primarily located in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres of the Earth.
 
• It is the largest and most populous continent, Asia is home to **diverse cultures**, landscapes, and historical significance.
 
• From the towering Himalayas to the sprawling Gobi Desert, Asia offers a kaleidoscope of experiences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Earth has **seven continents**, each with its own unique characteristics and fascinating details. Here's a glimpse into each of them:

**Africa**:

 
• The second-largest continent, Africa is renowned for its vibrant wildlife, rich cultural heritage, and stunning natural beauty.
 
• From the vast savannas of the Serengeti to the towering peaks of the Atlas Mountains, Africa is a land of endless discovery.

**North America**:

 
• This continent is known for its diverse landscapes, ranging from the towering mountains of Alaska to the sun-drenched beaches of California.
 
• North America is also a melting pot of cultures and ethnicities, making it a vibrant and dynamic region.

**South America:**

 
• Home to the Amazon rainforest, the Andes Mountains, and the vibrant cultures of Brazil and Argentina, South America is a continent teeming with life and natural beauty.
 
• From the ancient ruins of Machu Picchu to the breathtaking Iguazu Falls, South America offers endless opportunities for exploration.

**Antarctica:**

 
• The frozen continent of Antarctica is a land of mystery and scientific exploration.
 
• Covered in a thick ice sheet, Antarctica is home to diverse penguin colonies, seals, and whales.
 
• It's also a crucial region for understanding climate change and the Earth's ecosystem.

**Europe:**

 
• The continent of Europe is steeped in history and culture.
 
• From the ancient ruins of Rome to the modern metropolises of London and Paris, Europe offers a rich tapestry of experiences.
 
• The continent is also known for its stunning natural beauty, with diverse landscapes ranging from the Alps to the Mediterranean Sea.

**Australia:**

 
• The smallest continent by landmass, Australia is an island nation renowned for its unique wildlife, vast outback, and stunning beaches.
 
• From the iconic Sydney Opera House to the Great Barrier Reef, Australia offers a unique blend of natural beauty and modern vibrancy.

questions.question: Roots absorb water and ______ from the soil.
questions.solution:
• Root is a part in vascular plants which is responsible for absorbing water and minerals from the soil which are then transported to the rest of the plant via conducting tissue called Xylem.
 
• Roots are also responsible for storage of food, vegetative reproduction and in providing support and anchorage to the plant.

questions.question: Which body part of fishes helps them to change directions and keep their body balance in water?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Fins and tail**__** **(also known as the caudal fin) are the locomotive organs in fishes as their movement helps the fishes to move, maintain balance and change directions underwater.
 
• They may be bony, cartilaginous or fibrous in nature.
 
• Fish have **scales** to protect the skin of the fish from attacks from predators, parasites and other injuries.
 
• **Fish gills** are organs that allow fish to breathe underwater. Most fish exchange gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide using gills that are protected under gill covers on both sides of the pharynx (throat).

questions.question: Which disease is caused by deficiency of vitamin C?
questions.solution:
• Scurvy is a disease that is caused by deficiency of Vitamin C in the body.
 
• It causes fatigue, pain in legs, swellings, ulcers in gums and even bleeding.

questions.question: Which mirror has a very wide field of view?
questions.solution: • While reflecting, convex mirror bends the incident ray which leads to the formation of smaller images. Due to the formation of small images, larger area can be covered by a convex mirror.

questions.question: What is the unit of conductance?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The measure of how easily current can flow through a material is termed as its **conductance**__.
 
• Mathematically, it is the reciprocal of resistance of a given material.
 
• __**The unit of Conductance is mho.**__

questions.question: In computers the data is stored in which forms?
questions.solution:
• Computers store data in binary form as it is the language that is understood by the computer.
 
• The processor converts the commands and information given by the user into binary data for the computer to execute them.
 
• Binary data is numerically represented by 0s and 1s.

questions.question: Which is the most abundant metal in the earth’s crust?
questions.solution:
• Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust as it makes up about 8% of it.
 
• It’s atomic number is 13 and it is in group 13 of the periodic table.

questions.question: Which metal melts in the palm?
questions.solution:
• Gallium is a metal which easily melts in the palms as its melting point is 29.76°C and the average human body temperature is 37°C.
 
• It’s atomic number is 31 and it belongs to group 13 of the periodic table.

questions.question: Nitrates, Phosphates, metals are examples of which type of impurities in sewage?
questions.solution:
• Inorganic compounds are compounds that do not have a carbon atom and are not obtained from living matter which is why they are non-biodegradable.
 
• Nitrates, phosphates and metals are all inorganic compounds that are found in sewage due to the disposal of untreated wastewater from industries into water bodies.

questions.question: What is Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana?
questions.solution:
• Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is a scheme that aims at providing life insurance to people between the ages of 18 to 50.
 
• It was launched in 2015.
 
• This scheme provides the individual with a maximum of 2 lakh rupees.

questions.question: Who among the following invented Electric Motor?
questions.solution:
• Electric motor is a device that is used to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• It was invented by Michael Faraday in 1821.

questions.question: Who won the 2017 Men’s Single Wimbledon Championship?
questions.solution:
• Roger Federer defeated Marin Cilic to win the 2017 Men's Single Wimbledon Championship on 16th July 2017.
 
• It was Federer's 8th Wimbledon title.

questions.question: ‘Hornbill Festival’ which is also called ‘the Festival of Festivals’ is celebrated in which state?
questions.solution:
• The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland every yearfrom December 1-10.
 
• This festival is a celebration of the heritage and culture of Nagaland.

questions.question: Who won the Man Booker International Prize 2017?
questions.solution:
• The Man Booker International Prize is given to the author of the most exceptional and creative literary work in that year.
 
• The title is given along with a cash prize if 50,000 euros which is shared by the author and the publisher.
 
• David Grossman won the Man Booker International Prize 2017 for his book A Horse Walks into a Bar which was first published in 2014.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book named ‘Indian Parliamentary Diplomacy’?
questions.solution:
• Indian Parliamentary Dilplomacy is a book by Meira Kumar who was a former Lok Sabha speaker.
 
• It details Meira Kumar’s experience in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: What is the name of joint bi-annual military exercise conducted by India and Russia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INDRA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **INDRA **is the joint bi-annual military exercise conducted by **India and Russia** with the aim of boosting their defence cooperation.
 
• It was started in 2003.
 
• Word INDRA is the representation of initials of participating countries.
 
• Exercise involves live firing drills, air defence, anti-submarines exercises.

questions.question: What is the economic bedrock of the India-Bhutan relationship?
questions.solution:
• The base of the bilateral relations between Bhutan and India is cooperation in hydro-electric power sector which began in 1961.
 
• As part of this cooperation, India provides Bhutan with financial support needed for building hydropower projects. In return, India imports cheap electricity from Bhutan.
